 Knicks vs. Timberwolves injury report: Jonathan Kuminga pops up for much-anticipated showdown
 Jonathan Kuminga has a chance to play a part in the Minnesota Timberwolves' home game against the New York Knicks.
 By Rishabh Bhatnagar • Nov 19, 2026 at 9:39 AM ET • 3 min read Add ClutchPoints on Google Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images The 11-4 Minnesota Timberwolves will host the 8-6 New York Knicks at Target Center on Thursday night for what is Karl-Anthony Towns’ first game against his former team as a defending champion. Both teams are looking for their third win on the trot and there is plenty of reason why this may turn out to be a highly entertaining affair.
 Minnesota are 7-2 at home this season, but enter this game with several injury concerns, per the official injury report . New York, meanwhile, are just 4-3 on the road but arrive without any injury concerns. Jalen Brunson has scored 69 points in his last two appearances and comes into this one after a 31-point performance against the Toronto Raptors. 
 Jonathan Kuminga has been listed as questionable for this game after sitting out of the Timberwolves’ victory over the Portland Trail Blazers as he continues his recovery from a right shoulder contusion. Zyon Pullin joins him on the questionable list with the likes of Jaylen Clark, Donte DiVincenzo and most importantly, Anthony Edwards all confirmed to be out for this one.
 Watch NBA games LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jonathan Kuminga's injury status vs. Knicks 
 Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Jonathan Kuminga is questionable for Thursday's game against the New York Knicks, which means Minnesota will take a decision closer to tip-off. Kuminga’s absence adds to a list of problems for the Timberwolves as they are also without their main man ANT. Still, they have managed to remain competitive in recent weeks and have actually won eight of their last nine games.
 That has been a result of contributions across the board. Ayo Dosunmu is averaging 18.6 points per game, followed by LaMelo Ball at 17.7 and Jaden McDaniels at 17.1. Dosunmu delivered a season-high 30 points in Tuesday's 106-105 win over Portland and may once again prove important especially if Kuminga sits out.
 Regardless, Minnesota have gone 8-3 since Edwards’ injury and will hope to continue their run against the defending champions. Karl-Anthony Towns’ return to Minnesota for the first time since winning the championship will also be a defining storyline of the game.
 He has averaged 21.2 points and 14.1 rebounds per game while shooting 54.5% from the field, and almost returned with a triple-double against Toronto, recording 16 points, 16 rebounds and eight assists.
 KAT has averaged 29 points, 14.3 rebounds and 3.7 assists while shooting 61.7% from the field and 56.3% from beyond the arc across his previous three meetings against Minnesota. However, the bigger fish to fry for the Timberwolves remains Brunson, who is going at 27 points and 5.9 assists per game so far this season. Much will depend on the Timberwolves’ ability to restrict New York’s offense especially in the glass, with Rudy Gobert’s interior presence set to play an important role in what can be expected to be a close contest.
 Knicks injury report 
 None
 Timberwolves injury report 
 Jonathan Kuminga: Questionable (right shoulder contusion)
 Article Continues Below Zyon Pullin: Questionable (right quadriceps contusion)
 Anthony Edwards: Out (right knee arthroscopy)
 Donte DiVincenzo: Out (right Achilles tendon repair/surgery)
 Jaylen Clark: Out (right hamstring strain)
 Joan Beringer: Available (face mask)
